chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Sammak, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you enter Mecca while you are a Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu'), look at the houses of Mecca, then cease the Talbiyah. And when you reach the boundary of the houses of Mecca that existed before that day, if you reach the 'Aqabah of the Madaniyyin, cease the Talbiyah. And upon you is the Tahleel, Takbir, and praising Allah your Lord as much as you can. And if you are Mufrid (performing Hajj al-Ifrad), do not cease the Talbiyah until the Day of Arafah at the decline of the sun. And if you are Mu'tamir (performing Umrah), cease the Talbiyah when you enter the Haram.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَة: The ritual declaration of 'Labbayk' recited during Hajj and Umrah
key_terms.زَوَال الشَّمْس: The decline of the sun (Dhuhr time)
key_terms.عَقَبَةَ الْمَدَنِيِّين: A specific location or boundary in Mecca associated with the people of Medina
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّع: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in the same season
key_terms.مُفْرِد: A pilgrim who performs only Hajj, without Umrah

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim stop reciting the Talbiyah during Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Istibsar*, highlighting the distinct jurisprudential markers for the three types of Hajj as taught by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The transition from the vocal declaration of *Talbiyah* to silent *Dhikr* and *Tasbih* signifies the pilgrim's shift from the state of *Ihram* to the state of *Hill* (freedom from certain restrictions), a key distinction in Shia fiqh. This hadith serves as a practical guide for pilgrims to synchronize their ritual declarations with the physical milestones of entering the sacred precincts.
